title: Two-orbit bonds, forgetting on the values states take, and exposure
claim: Theorem K: the least bond of any size inside an orbit at level k and one at level k + s, read from their exact joint, bounds L at every depth; Theorem F': forgetting read on actual joints from level k forces growth; Lemma E: an exposed missing pair gives a two-orbit bond. Computed: the four non-direct census patterns that never forget are bounded at every depth (4, 4, 5, 6), so forgetting decides all 786 small-orbit census descriptions; in 2,380 fresh and mutated patterns, 39 never forget on all values without a two-orbit bond: 14 forget on actual values, 13 have top joints that become products (one grows past its parent at depth 11), 12 keep a hidden dependence. Conjecture C' open. Referee pending.
failure_conditions: A two-orbit bond from the joint that is not a bond of the pattern.
A pattern forgetting on actual values whose reach is below 1 + ceil(s/r).
An exposed missing pair with no two-orbit bond.
remaining_obligations: Conjecture C' (no persistent two-orbit bond from the top implies growth): open on 25 patterns.
foundation_claim_scope: The plain not-all-equal law; addressed patterns placed by automaton maps, knots within a level or between adjacent levels.

validation.independence: Written by Claude 2026-11-17; the advisor reviewed the design and proposed the exposure lemma; referee pending.
validation.status: proof by hand plus finite computation; check passed
